item.title: CCTV captures attempted vehicle break-in at Bayview Heights
item.description: Another attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday. The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.
item.content:encoded:
Another attempted break-in has been reported at Bayview Heights after CCTV footage captured an intruder attempting to break into a vehicle at around 3am on Thursday.

The vehicle owner, Rash Jehad, says on social media that they woke up after hearing the alarm and found the intruder still attempting to gain entry.

According to Jehad, the intruder appeared unfazed by the alarm and only ran away after they shouted at him.

He says they contacted Nabua Police Station multiple times for assistance during the incident but claims there was no response.

The incident has raised concerns over the safety and security of residents in the area and the response to calls for police assistance during the early hours of the morning.

item.title: Nadi father raises concern over Lautoka Hospital bed shortage affecting 17-year-old son who needs CT scan
item.description: A Nadi father has raised serious concerns after his 17-year-old son, who requires further medical assessment, was unable to be transferred to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan because there was no available bed. Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm on Friday, and doctors planned to transfer him to the Lautoka hospital for a CT scan.
item.content:encoded:
A Nadi father has raised serious concerns after his 17-year-old son, who requires further medical assessment, was unable to be transferred to Lautoka Hospital for a CT scan because there was no available bed.

Mohammed Kalam says his son was admitted to Nadi Hospital at around 5pm on Friday, and doctors planned to transfer him to the Lautoka hospital for a CT scan.

However, Kalam says the family was later informed that there was no spare bed available.

He says the same explanation has been given repeatedly since Friday.

Kalam says the situation is particularly concerning for his family as they live in Nadi and are waiting for his son to receive the required medical attention.

Kalam has questioned why the necessary hospital resources are not available to accommodate patients requiring specialised care.

Insert: Kalam - What is Health Minister doing Aug 16

Questions have been sent to the Minister for Health Dr Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu regarding the delay and the availability of beds for patients requiring specialised care.

item.title: Resident raises concerns over drinking and vandalism at Samabula church
item.description: A 24-year-old resident is raising concerns over repeated incidents of drinking, vandalism and damage at the Central Revival Centre church, located in Komo Park Ground, Samabula. Speaking to fijivillage News, he says groups of young people gather at the church premises and consume alcohol, despite such activities being prohibited in the area.
item.content:encoded:
A 24-year-old resident is raising concerns over repeated incidents of drinking, vandalism and damage at the Central Revival Centre church, located in Komo Park Ground, Samabula.

Speaking to fijivillage News, he says groups of young people gather at the church premises and consume alcohol, despite such activities being prohibited in the area.

He says water pipes at the church are frequently damaged as well , and church members later have to repair them.

The 24-year-old also says trees have been cut down and systems at the back of the church have been damaged.

He is calling on authorities and relevant stakeholders to take action.

He says the last report was lodged six months ago, however, no action was taken.

item.title: You cannot claim to love Fiji while littering the land – Dr Ahmed Shariff
item.description: Fiji Medical Association Treasurer Dr Ahmed Shakeel Shariff says Fijians cannot proudly call Fiji home while continuing to litter and damage the very environment they claim to love. Dr Shariff says it is difficult to understand why some people continue to dump rubbish on beaches, streets and in their neighbourhoods when rubbish simply belongs in a rubbish bin.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji Medical Association Treasurer Dr Ahmed Shakeel Shariff says Fijians cannot proudly call Fiji home while continuing to litter and damage the very environment they claim to love.

Dr Shariff says it is difficult to understand why some people continue to dump rubbish on beaches, streets and in their neighbourhoods when rubbish simply belongs in a rubbish bin.

Insert: Shariff on Noqu Viti, Noqu Kalou 16th Aug 26

He says littering is damaging the beautiful and serene environment Fiji is known for and could deny future generations the opportunity to enjoy the same surroundings that people enjoy today.

Dr Shariff says rubbish also makes the environment dangerous for children to play and run around in and is making the country that people describe as heaven “not so heavenly”.

He is urging authorities to ensure there are sufficient rubbish bins in municipal areas and that rubbish is properly and regularly collected.

Dr Shariff says waste management should not only cover general rubbish but green waste as well, as people need proper collection services to keep their homes and yards clean .

He says keeping communities clean is also important for public health and can help prevent diseases, viruses and mosquito-borne illnesses such as dengue.

Dr Shariff is also calling on parents to teach their children not to throw rubbish and says adults must practise what they teach by disposing of their own rubbish properly.

He says people should also demand timely action from the relevant authorities when rubbish bins are not cleared or cleaned, or when bins are damaged and need attention.

Dr Shariff adds that littering and waste management remain major problems in the country, and protecting Fiji requires people to take responsibility for their own actions.

item.title: Police investigate daylight break-in in Valelevu, suspects yet to be arrested
item.description: An investigation is ongoing into a daylight break-in in Valelevu, where three young men forced their way into a house yesterday morning. All three were seen on CCTV trying to force open the door to enter the house and were later seen leaving with a carton of goods.
item.content:encoded:
An investigation is ongoing into a daylight break-in in Valelevu, where three young men forced their way into a house yesterday morning.

All three were seen on CCTV trying to force open the door to enter the house and were later seen leaving with a carton of goods.

Businessman Watsoni Nata Junior posted the CCTV footage, which shows three men breaking into his neighbour’s home.

Police have confirmed to fijivillage News that they are investigating the incident and that the suspects have not yet been arrested.

Nata has also raised concerns about people having the confidence to turn up at someone’s home in broad daylight and break in.

He says these are people’s homes and neighbourhoods, and everyone has a role to play in looking out for one another.

Anyone who recognises the three men shown in the CCTV footage or has information that could assist in identifying them is being urged to provide the information directly to Police.

item.title: Tuinaceva to follow up with FRA on proposed Sote-Namalata Bridge
item.description: Assistant Minister for Public Works and Transport, Naisa Tuinaceva says he will follow up with the Fiji Roads Authority on the proposed bridge at the Sote Village crossing towards Namalata, as students have to cross the river daily to get to school. When fijivillage News raised the issue, Tuinaceva says the road and water concerns raised by the Namalata district representative are also being looke
item.content:encoded:
Assistant Minister for Public Works and Transport, Naisa Tuinaceva says he will follow up with the Fiji Roads Authority on the proposed bridge at the Sote Village crossing towards Namalata, as students have to cross the river daily to get to school.

When fijivillage News raised the issue, Tuinaceva says the road and water concerns raised by the Namalata district representative are also being looked into.

Tuinaceva says the Namalata district representative also raised concerns about several other areas that require attention, and these will be looked into.

Meanwhile, he says one of the issues raised was the condition of the road to Matacaucau, and they had committed to addressing it through FRA.

Tuinaceva says FRA carried out work on the road the very next day.

He says when complaints and concerns are raised, FRA considers them alongside its normal programme of works .

He says issues raised at the Tikina level and then at the provincial level are normally discussed with relevant government agencies, particularly FRA.

Tuinaceva believes scoping work for the proposed project may have already been carried out and says work should begin once everything is ready.
